Even with those offsets, the added Barbiturate, the less negative minimum partial charge, and the more saturated, ring-containing shape keep this neighbor aligned with BBB crossing.

Neighbor 4 is one of the negative-labeled neighbors, but its comparison still contains several features that favor the crossing class relative to the query. Since this neighbor already sits near the upper end of the common CNS-favorable PSA region, the query’s lower PSA and cleaner scaffold make it look more BBB-compatible than the negative label of the neighbor itself.

Neighbor 6 is the strongest negative-labeled analog in terms of some polarity descriptors, but it also points toward the crossing class once the full comparison is considered. The neighbor, however, has an estimated logD of -2.809 compared with 1.4579 for the query, so the query is much more lipophilic at physiological conditions; that large increase in logD is treated as unfavorable in this specific comparison even though moderate ionization-aware lipophilicity can matter for BBB penetration. The repeated presence of Barbiturate in the query, the generally favorable minimum partial charge comparisons, the removal of acidic or highly polar motifs in some of the negative neighbors, and the added aliphatic carbocycle/sp3 character together outweigh the local disadvantages. Taken as a whole, these nearest-neighbor comparisons support option (B): crosses the BBB.
